title: Relative endomorphism planar operad of a coherent functor
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, cores and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the infinity category $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ of [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration], its cartesian operadic envelope of [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope], and ordinary nonsymmetric infinity operads over $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ as defined in [lem-coef-nonsymmetric-operads-presentability]. All categories and functor categories fit in fixed containing universes. Let $f:A\to B$ be any coherent functor. For each $r\geq0$, choose a replete full subcategory $C_r\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(B^r,B)$, where replete means closed under equivalence. Assume $\mathrm{id}_B\in C_1$ and that $v\in C_k$ and $w_i\in C_{r_i}$ imply $v(w_1,\ldots,w_k)\in C_{r_1+\cdots+r_k}$, using consecutive disjoint input lists, including empty lists.

Form the one-color endomorphism planar operad $E_A$ by restricting the cartesian envelope of $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ to tuples of the object $A$ and to ordered blocks. Similarly form the endomorphism planar operad of the object $f$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\operatorname{Cat}_\infty)$ with its pointwise cartesian product. Retain precisely those operations whose target-endpoint functor belongs to the corresponding $C_r$; call the resulting operation suboperad $E_C(f)$. The analogous restriction of the endomorphism planar operad of $B$ is denoted $E_C(B)$. These constructions give ordinary nonsymmetric infinity operads and endpoint morphisms
$$E_A\xleftarrow{p}E_C(f)\xrightarrow{q}E_C(B).$$
Their fixed-color $r$-ary operation spaces are naturally
$$E_A(r)=\operatorname{Fun}(A^r,A)^\simeq,\qquad E_C(B)(r)=C_r^\simeq,$$
$$E_C(f)(r)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(A^r,A)^\simeq\mathop{\times}^{h}_{\operatorname{Fun}(A^r,B)^\simeq}C_r^\simeq,$$
where the maps to the middle space are $u\mapsto fu$ and $v\mapsto vf^r$. Thus an operation is $(u,v,\eta)$ with $\eta:vf^r\simeq fu$; $p$ and $q$ retain $u$ and $v$. Substitution uses disjoint ordered blocks and pastes these natural equivalences. The unary identity is $(\mathrm{id}_A,\mathrm{id}_B,\mathrm{id}_f)$, and arity zero is included. For a base arrow $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$, let $a=\alpha^{\mathrm{op}}:[m]\to[n]$ and $s_j=a(j)-a(j-1)$. Between the tuple objects of either of these one-color operads, the mapping space over $\alpha$ is the product of its operation spaces of arities $s_j$, $1\leq j\leq m$, with empty product a point. The total mapping space is the disjoint union of these spaces over base arrows. The endpoint maps respect these formulas and all substitution simplices.

Let $J$ be the identity-only one-color planar operad, with just the unary identity as single-output operation, and let $\mathsf{Ass}_{\mathrm{pl}}=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ be the planar associative operad with its unique operation in each arity, including zero. Derived operadic mapping spaces under $J$ fix the color together with its identification; they do not quotient the underlying object by its automorphisms. The space $\operatorname{Map}_{J/}(\mathsf{Ass}_{\mathrm{pl}},E_A)$ is the space of unital planar operation systems on the fixed category $A$ in the sense of [lem-coef-monoidal-block-projection-coherence], with unary identity identified with $\mathrm{id}_A$. The corresponding mapping space with target $E_C(f)$ is the space of such systems on $A$ and $B$, with every $B$-operation in $C_r$, together with coherent natural equivalences along the fixed functor $f$ making it a morphism of systems. The endpoint maps forget to the two systems. Evaluation at the arity-$r$ corolla is exactly evaluation to the operation spaces just displayed. These identifications include all tree contraction, grafting, identity and nullary coherences, commute with additional simplicial parameters, and identify homotopy fibers with spaces of these data equipped with their specified identifications.

source.place: Agent-formulated arrow-endomorphism construction using HA Remark 2.1.3.4 (pointwise monoidal functor categories), section 2.4.1 (cartesian structures), and Definitions 4.1.3.2, 4.1.3.9, 4.1.3.16 (planar operads and associative sections). These places were read online; the relative operation-suboperad formula and fixed-color mapping-space interpretation are the explicit auxiliary assertion, not a verbatim theorem of HA. Archive WANTED in report.md; no Stacks tag states this quasicategorical construction.

proof.text: Put $D=\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ and $H=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,D)$. The finite products in $D$ are products of categories, including $*=\Delta^0$, by [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. By [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration] and [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], $\operatorname{Map}_D(X,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(X,Y)^\simeq$, naturally in $X,Y$ and compatibly with composition. The functor category $H$ is a quasicategory by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. These statements apply in containing universes, so neither $A$ nor $B$ needs internal finite products.

source.place: Sections 2.4.1-2.4.2; Cat_infinity convention and coherent-nerve mapping comparison supplied by the cited nodes.

proof.text: For arrows $g_i:X_i\to Y_i$ in $D$, take their product arrow $g:\prod_iX_i\to\prod_iY_i$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-morphism-square] to an arbitrary test arrow $h:U\to V$. Its three mapping-space factors for $\operatorname{Map}_H(h,g)$ are products of the corresponding factors for the $g_i$, by the product property in $D$. In the path model in that node, a point, a path, and every higher simplex in a finite product are exactly a tuple of such data. Therefore the comparison induced by the product projections is $\operatorname{Map}_H(h,g)\simeq\prod_i\operatorname{Map}_H(h,g_i)$. For the empty family all three factors and their path pullback are points. This proves the product universal property in $H$ and shows that both endpoint evaluations preserve finite products. In particular $f^{\times r}$ has endpoints $A^r,B^r$, with arrow $f^r$, including $f^0:\ast\to\ast$.

source.place: Remark 2.1.3.4; explicit product verification from the already stated interval-arrow mapping formula.

proof.text:
For $T=D$ or $H$ form $T^\times$ by [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope], then pull back along the ordered-block map $\operatorname{Cut}:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{Fin}_*$ specified in [lem-coef-cartesian-associative-segal-comparison] (forgetting its ordered-fiber decoration). Base change is a cocartesian fibration by [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. For $x=A,B,f$, take the full simplicial subcategory on the tuple $x^{[n]}=(x,\ldots,x)$ in each degree. Full subcategories are quasicategories by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Inner horn lifts over the base stay in this full subcategory, because all vertices already belong to it. The envelope formula restricts to
$$\operatorname{Map}^{\alpha}(x^{[n]},x^{[m]})\simeq\prod_{j=1}^m\operatorname{Map}_T(x^{s_j},x),\quad s_j=a(j)-a(j-1).$$
The fiber in degree $n$ has one tuple object and mapping space the $n$th power of the unary mapping space; inert projections give the Segal equivalence, also for $n=0$. An inert arrow with identity singleton blocks gives a lift between the retained tuples. Its cocartesian mapping square is the coordinate identity on the displayed products, so [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] proves it is still cocartesian after restriction. The same product formula is the relative-limit axiom of [lem-coef-nonsymmetric-operads-presentability]. Thus these full tuple restrictions are ordinary nonsymmetric infinity operads.

source.place: Construction 4.1.2.9; section 2.4.1 and Definition 4.1.3.2; direct verification of the tuple restriction.

proof.text: In the $B$ tuple operad mark an edge over $\alpha$ as retained when each of its output block operations belongs to $C_{s_j}$. Fullness and repleteness imply that $C_r^\simeq$ is a union of components in $\operatorname{Fun}(B^r,B)^\simeq$: any path is a natural equivalence, so its other endpoint belongs to $C_r$, and fullness includes every higher simplex between such endpoints. The retained edges contain identities since $\mathrm{id}_B\in C_1$. They are closed under composition: the component at output $j$ of a composite substitutes the consecutive output operations feeding $j$ into its outer operation, and the stated closure assumption places that functor in $C_{a(b(j))-a(b(j-1))}$. This follows because the block lengths sum to $a(b(j))-a(b(j-1))$. Inputs outside the relevant interval are discarded, not substituted a second time. This includes an outer nullary operation and any empty inner block. Any equivalent representative of the composite is retained by repleteness.

source.place: Ordered-block formula of Construction 4.1.2.9; composition formula of section 2.4.1, with the given C_r hypotheses.

proof.text: Define $E_C(B)$ to contain precisely the simplices all of whose edges are retained in step 4. This is a simplicial subset. Given an inner horn over a base simplex, fill it in the $B$ tuple operad. If its dimension is at least three, every edge of the filler is already an edge of the horn. In dimension two the only new edge is a composite, and step 4 shows it is retained. Thus the restricted projection is an inner fibration. Its mapping spaces over $\alpha$ are precisely the unions of components with the retained blocks, hence $\prod_j C_{s_j}^\simeq$; this assertion can also be checked in the right-pinched model, where all edges except the varying operation edges are identities. Identity singleton-block inert lifts are retained. Precomposing along such a lift changes only the names of the same consecutive blocks, so on each base-arrow fiber it is the identity of these products. By [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] these are cocartesian lifts in the restriction. The degree-$n$ fiber is the $n$th power of the unary fiber, and the displayed product gives the relative-limit axiom. These verify every condition in [lem-coef-nonsymmetric-operads-presentability], without assuming that the subcategory is full on unary operations.

source.place: Definitions 4.1.3.2 and 4.1.3.9; agent-written edge-restriction horn and Segal verification.

proof.text: The two endpoint evaluations $H\to D$ preserve products by step 2, so [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope] gives their coherent envelope functors, and restriction to tuples gives endpoint operad maps. Define $E_C(f)$ as the inverse image of the edge restriction defining $E_C(B)$ under target evaluation. Its inner horn fillers stay in this inverse image: for dimensions at least three all edges were supplied, and for dimension two the new target block is the retained composite of step 4. Its inert identity-block lifts are retained and its mapping products and Segal maps are the inverse-image products of step 3. The same cocartesian mapping-square check as in step 5 applies, using [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. Hence it is an ordinary nonsymmetric infinity operad by [lem-coef-nonsymmetric-operads-presentability]. For an arbitrary inert cocartesian edge, its output blocks are invertible unary operations in the restricted unary category: compare its mapping square with the identity-block lift, over identity base arrows; the resulting precomposition equivalence gives an inverse in each unary factor. Conversely such inverses make every block mapping square an equivalence. Endpoint evaluation preserves these inverses, so it preserves all inert cocartesian edges. Thus restriction gives $p:E_C(f)\to E_A$ and $q:E_C(f)\to E_C(B)$.

source.place: Remark 2.1.3.4 and Definition 4.1.3.9; inverse-image operation restriction.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-morphism-square] to the arrows $f^r:A^r\to B^r$ and $f:A\to B$ in $D$. With the mapping-space identification of step 1 it gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_H(f^r,f)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(A^r,A)^\simeq\times^h_{\operatorname{Fun}(A^r,B)^\simeq}\operatorname{Fun}(B^r,B)^\simeq.$$
The two maps are $u\mapsto fu$ and $v\mapsto vf^r$. The cited equivalence respects the joint endpoint projection, so restricting its second coordinate to the union of components $C_r^\simeq$ gives exactly the asserted operation space of $E_C(f)$. Reversing its path coordinate if necessary writes it as $\eta:vf^r\simeq fu$. The unrestricted $A$ case and restricted $B$ case give the other two displayed operation spaces. Substitution in step 3 now gives all the asserted over-$\alpha$ product formulas. Since the mapping space in the ordinary base $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is discrete, its fibers give the asserted disjoint-union formula for the total mapping space, including the empty output product.

source.place: Remark 2.1.3.4; Kerodon Tag 06BZ, the cited interval-arrow Hom formula, specialized to Cat_infinity.

proof.text:
Write an outer operation as $(u,v,\eta:vf^k\simeq fu)$ and its inner operations as $(u_i,v_i,\eta_i:v_if^{r_i}\simeq fu_i)$. Their composite has endpoints $u(u_1,\ldots,u_k)$ and $v(v_1,\ldots,v_k)$, and its comparison is the path
$$v(v_1f^{r_1},\ldots,v_kf^{r_k})\xRightarrow{v(\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_k)}v(fu_1,\ldots,fu_k)\xRightarrow{\eta(u_1,\ldots,u_k)}fu(u_1,\ldots,u_k).$$
These are the restrictions of product and composition in $H$, as follows from the natural joint-endpoint comparison in [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-morphism-square] and the substitution formula of [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope]. Thus all higher substitution simplices are those of that envelope, rather than independently chosen pasting homotopies. The unary unit is its degenerate identity square $(\mathrm{id}_A,\mathrm{id}_B,\mathrm{id}_f)$. If $k=0$ the first path uses the empty family and the second is the given nullary comparison. Endpoint evaluation restricts the very same simplices to their $u$ and $v$ coordinates, so it respects substitution in every dimension.

source.place: Remark 2.1.3.4 and section 2.4.1; explicit pasting formula inside the already constructed arrow envelope.

proof.text: For $T=D,H$, first allow the color object $x\in T$ to vary. Apply [lem-coef-colored-operation-section-reconstruction] to the ordinary symmetric associative operad and the pullback of $T^\times$ to its operator category. The fibers, cocartesian lifts and output Segal formulas required there are the envelope formulas in step 3. Its operation data at $x$ are maps $x^r\to x$ and all tree compatibilities. Equivalently restrict to planar sections by [lem-coef-cartesian-associative-segal-comparison]; this equivalence preserves the underlying object and all higher families. The ordered extension needed in the symmetric reconstruction merely reindexes each product into the operation's specified order: contraction concatenates those lists, so it recovers the same planar tree data and introduces no extra symmetry on $t_r$. At $x=A$ in $D$, maps $A^r\to A$ are functors and coherence paths are natural equivalences by step 1. Hence the reconstructed data are exactly the unital planar operation systems of [lem-coef-monoidal-block-projection-coherence]. For $x=f$ in $H$, step 7 identifies each operation with a triple $(u,v,\eta)$, and step 8 identifies its substitution. Consequently these reconstructed data are exactly two such systems and a coherent morphism along $f$. Requiring their target operations to lie in $C_r$ is precisely factorization through the restriction of step 6, since its higher simplices are retained whenever their operation edges are retained.

source.place: Definitions 4.1.3.16 and 4.1.3.9; reconstruction and associative--planar comparison with all parameter families.

proof.text: Now impose the fixed color with its identification. The identity-only operad $J$ has tuple objects and only identity singleton-output components (its operator category is the inert subcategory of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$); in particular it has no nullary single-output operation. An inert-preserving map from $J$ records a color and its inert tuple identifications. In the reconstruction theorem [lem-coef-colored-operation-section-reconstruction], these identifications have a contractible space of extensions once the color and its identification are specified. Therefore restriction to $J$ is the underlying-color functor on the cores of the section categories of step 9. The mapping space under $J$ is its homotopy fiber at the specified map $J\to E$: explicitly it consists of an operadic map $\mathsf{Ass}_{\mathrm{pl}}\to E$ and an identification of its restriction with that specified map, with every higher simplex of this identification. This is the dual comma mapping-space formula of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], applied in the operad infinity category of [lem-coef-nonsymmetric-operads-presentability] to the one-point diagram at $J$. Thus it fixes $A$, respectively the arrow $f$, with its chosen identification. It does not take the quotient of the structure space by the equivalences of that object. Combining this fiber description with step 9 gives both claimed mapping-space interpretations, including the identified unary identity.

source.place: Definitions 4.1.3.9 and 4.1.3.16; agent-written fixed-color undercategory interpretation using the cited comma formula.

proof.text: The reconstruction statement [lem-coef-colored-operation-section-reconstruction] explicitly includes arbitrary simplicial parameters, restriction of parameters, projection to colors, and contractible spaces of reconstructions with their specified identifications. The comparison [lem-coef-cartesian-associative-segal-comparison] identifies the standard $r$-input operation with the active endpoint-preserving arrow $[r]\to[1]$, also for $r=0$. Thus its corolla evaluation here is precisely the projection to step 7's operation space. All endpoint maps are induced by endpoint evaluation, so they forget to the two systems. Applying these parameter-compatible equivalences to a diagram and to a point with its specified identification identifies their homotopy fibers, by the path model of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. This retains the tree contractions, graftings and identity/nullary data already supplied by reconstruction, with their whole higher simplices.

source.place: Section 4.1.3; parameter and corolla clauses of the cited reconstruction/comparison statements.

proof.text: No existence of a nullary operation was presumed. If $C_0$ is empty, the restricted nullary space is empty and the corresponding space of unital systems is empty. If $A=\varnothing$, then $E_A(0)=\operatorname{Fun}(*,\varnothing)^\simeq=\varnothing$, again excluding unital systems without excluding the operad. For an arbitrary $f$ the construction itself still exists, even when an operation-space homotopy pullback is empty. For an output-free base arrow, all mapping products are points; for $r=1$ the specified degenerate identity lies in the restriction by the hypothesis on $C_1$. Thus no nonemptiness, equivalence, full faithfulness, presentability, or internal-product hypothesis on $f,A,B$ has entered.

source.place: Boundary-case verification of the displayed construction.
